fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile and fracture testing, whereas the target concerns composition screening in the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W system and room-temperature compression of as-cast Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5.

It replaces the target intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation, VEC/density screening of 38,326 compositions, and alloy fabrication—with an image-based neural-network proposal that was not part of the reported work.
The proposed mechanism based on image-learned stress concentrations does not reconstruct the target VEC–Peierls-barrier–dislocation-mobility mechanism.
The claimed 15–20% accuracy improvement and order-of-magnitude computational saving are unsupported by cited data or a defined prior-method benchmark.
No supporting prior evidence is supplied despite the request for it.
explanation: The response is a generic, prospectively testable image-based ML proposal, but it does not scientifically match the hidden study. It misses the alloy system, selected composition, screening variables, as-cast condition, compression protocol, baseline alloy, mechanism, and measured outcomes. In particular, it omits the observed 35.7% compressive fracture strain, 1115 MPa yield strength, and 2550 MPa compressive strength relative to equimolar NbMoTaVW. Its boundary statement appropriately notes distribution shift and unmodeled defect mechanisms, and the blinded holdout supplies some falsifiability. However, splitting nominally similar samples from one processing population risks sample-level leakage and does not test transfer across independent batches or processing states. The accuracy and speed thresholds are arbitrary, conventional comparators are not operationally standardized, and no evidence supports the numerical gains.
